title: Telegram Bot API transport (net/http, long polling)
description:
New package internal/operator/telegram implementing operator.Channel. The ONLY package where Telegram API types appear. Raw net/http + encoding/json — no new go.mod dependencies.

- Client with configurable BaseURL (default https://api.telegram.org, overridable for tests / A31 evidence).
- Methods: GetMe, SendMessage (HTML parse mode, InlineKeyboardMarkup, ForceReply), EditMessageText, EditMessageReplyMarkup, AnswerCallbackQuery, GetUpdates (long poll: timeout param, offset advance, allowed_updates=message,callback_query).
- Bound-user filter: updates whose sender/from.id differs from configured user_id are dropped at this layer (fact A14 transport half).
- Map interface types → Telegram wire types: Question options → callback_data ids (≤64 bytes; short ids, labels stay local), multi-select → toggle keyboard + Done button, allow-other → Other… button switching to ForceReply.
- fakebot subpackage: httptest server speaking enough Bot API for tests (getMe, sendMessage capture, getUpdates fed from a script queue, edit/answer capture) — shared by T4 pairing tests and epic 2.

Test cases (against fakebot):
- GetUpdates advances offset; long-poll timeout returns empty slice, no error.
- Update from wrong user_id is dropped; right user_id becomes an Event.
- AskDeliver for each shape produces correct reply_markup JSON; callback_data ≤64 bytes.
- Resolve edits message text and clears reply_markup.
Run: go test -short -count=1 ./internal/operator/...
acceptance_criteria: All telegram transport tests pass against fakebot; operator.Channel satisfied; no telegram import outside internal/operator/telegram (grep-checkable)
